commands:
chmod +x scripts/sync.sh
mkdir -p notes /tmp/sync-test && echo a > notes/a.txt && echo b > notes/b.txt
./scripts/sync.sh /tmp/sync-test && echo "--- non-verbose exit: $?"
./scripts/sync.sh --verbose /tmp/sync-test && echo "--- verbose exit: $?"
ls /tmp/sync-test
turns.final:
Done. `scripts/sync.sh` now accepts an optional `--verbose` flag as its first argument, which prints `copied: <file>` for each file:

- `./scripts/sync.sh /path/to/dest` — unchanged behavior, silent
- `./scripts/sync.sh --verbose /path/to/dest` — prints each copied file
- The flag is shifted off so `$dest` parsing still works, and POSIX `if` is used (instead of `[ ] && echo`) to avoid a nonzero exit status in non-verbose mode

Verified both modes run cleanly with exit 0.
